name: Euro-area economy
summary: Euro-area GDP grew 0.4% in Q3 and the final October composite PMI was 51.7; November flash PMIs due 23 Nov
state: Eurostat estimated euro-area GDP growth of 0.4% in the third quarter, confirmed in its second estimate on 13 Nov (Eurostat). The HCOB composite PMI was revised to 51.7 in October from a 51.9 flash, a four-month low but above 50, as France slipped back into contraction (S&P Global; Finanznachrichten, 4 Nov). November flash PMIs had not been published as of 21 Nov and are due on 23 Nov, so the latest data remain consistent with Normal.
for_you: Growth is positive but slowing; French businesses are already contracting. Workers and firms in energy-intensive industries remain most exposed if high gas prices persist into winter.
rubric_hit: Normal: Q3 GDP +0.4% and composite PMI 51.7 > 50; Watch would need GDP ~0 or PMI 45–50

sources.title: Eurostat — GDP up by 0.4% in the euro area and by 0.5% in the EU
S&P Global — Eurozone flash PMI: growth spurt wanes amid renewed French downturn
Finanznachrichten — Eurozone private sector growth moderates

why: The euro area is the UK's largest trading partner; stagnation there hits UK exports and European markets.
drivers: Energy prices, German industry, ECB policy, fiscal rules, China demand.

rubric.alert: Technical recession, or PMI < 45, or bond-spread fragmentation forcing ECB action.
rubric.normal: Positive GDP growth and composite PMI > 50.
